records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the whole chapter is one long picture: Jerusalem as an abandoned baby girl whom the LORD rescued, raised and married, and who then became an unfaithful wife
decisions.reason: The chapter tells the story of Jerusalem from birth to judgment and then to restoration. The LORD finds a newborn girl left to die (verses 3-7), takes her as his wife when she is grown (verses 8-14), and she turns to other lovers (verses 15-34). She is judged as an adulterous wife (verses 35-43), compared with her "sisters" Samaria and Sodom (verses 44-58), and finally given an everlasting covenant (verses 59-63). The picture of the covenant as a marriage and of idolatry as unfaithfulness comes from the earlier prophets (Hosea 1-3; Jeremiah 2:2; 3:1-10). Chapter 23 tells a similar story about two sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Literal follows the Hebrew's frank language; Balanced and Readable state its meaning plainly and soberly. The whole chapter is marked for careful human review.
alternatives: Balanced and Readable soften the sexual language
every level reproduces the Hebrew word for word
decisions.reason: The chapter describes Jerusalem's unfaithfulness in explicit sexual terms, and its judgment as the public shaming of an adulterous wife. The project's rule for this chapter and chapter 23 is that Literal follows the Hebrew, and Balanced and Readable say what the Hebrew means plainly: they do not blur it with vague words, they do not make it cruder than the Hebrew, and they add no detail it does not have. Where the Hebrew uses a polite word for the body (such as "feet" in verse 25 or "flesh" in verse 26), Literal keeps it and Balanced and Readable state its meaning soberly. The verb *zanah* is "prostitute oneself" at Literal and Balanced and "be unfaithful, like a woman with many lovers" at Readable, as Judges 2:17 and Jeremiah 3:1 (see verse 15). This decision is marked uncertain so that a named human reviewer checks the wording of the whole chapter before any of it is approved.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set for the prophets in the Jeremiah table, which Ezekiel keeps.

records.heading: Jerusalem, the abandoned child and the unfaithful wife

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הוֹדַ֥ע אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אֶת־תּוֹעֲבֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations,
pieces: Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her detestable practices,

L.2: Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations,

R.2: Son of man, make Jerusalem see the disgusting things she has done.

decisions.choice: son of man: a human being, a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: This is how God addresses Ezekiel throughout the book; see the note at 2:1. It stresses that Ezekiel is a mortal standing before God.

decisions.choice: her abominations: the practices that make her hateful to the LORD, above all the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: The word *to'evah* is used for what the LORD finds repulsive: idolatry, child sacrifice and other practices of the nations (Deuteronomy 18:9-12). The chapter goes on to list them.

decisions.choice: abominations (L); detestable practices (B); disgusting things (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *to'evah* in Ezekiel; see the main note at 5:9.

decisions.choice: confront Jerusalem with (B); make Jerusalem see (R)
decisions.reason: "Make known" here means to bring her own deeds before her so that she must face them, not to tell her something she does not know.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מְכֹרֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ וּמֹ֣לְדֹתַ֔יִךְ מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י אָבִ֥יךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י וְאִמֵּ֥ךְ חִתִּֽית׃
records.gloss: and you will say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to Jerusalem: Your origins and your birth [were] from [the] land of the Canaanite; your father [was] the Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.
pieces: and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to Jerusalem: You came from the land of the Canaanites; that is where you were born. Your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.

L.3: and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to Jerusalem: Your origins and your birth [were] from the land of the Canaanites; your father [was] the Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.

R.3: Tell her, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to Jerusalem: You were born in the land of Canaan. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.

decisions.choice: your father an Amorite, your mother a Hittite: Jerusalem's ancestry is that of the peoples of Canaan, not of Abraham
alternatives: Ezekiel is giving the actual descent of the city's population
decisions.reason: The Amorites and Hittites are named among the peoples who lived in Canaan before Israel (Genesis 15:16-21; Deuteronomy 7:1). Jerusalem was a Canaanite city, held by the Jebusites, until David took it (2 Samuel 5:6-9), so in a sense its history did begin among these peoples. But the point is its character: from its birth the city has been like the nations whose practices the LORD condemned (Leviticus 18:24-28). Verse 45 takes up the same parents again.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem addressed as a woman: the city stands for its people
decisions.reason: In Hebrew a city is feminine, and the prophets often speak to a city as a woman (Isaiah 1:21; Jeremiah 3:1-3). Here the whole story of the nation is told as the life of one woman. The "you" throughout the chapter is feminine.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula for *koh 'amar* with *Adonai YHWH*. Under the quotation rule for Ezekiel, neither the LORD's words to Ezekiel nor the message he is told to give take quotation marks; only human speech quoted inside them takes double quotes.

records.source: וּמוֹלְדוֹתַ֗יִךְ בְּי֨וֹם הוּלֶּ֤דֶת אֹתָךְ֙ לֹֽא־כָרַּ֣ת שָׁרֵּ֔ךְ וּבְמַ֥יִם לֹֽא־רֻחַ֖צְתְּ לְמִשְׁעִ֑י וְהָמְלֵ֨חַ֙ לֹ֣א הֻמְלַ֔חַתְּ וְהָחְתֵּ֖ל לֹ֥א חֻתָּֽלְתְּ׃
records.gloss: And [as for] your birth, on [the] day you were born not was cut your umbilical cord, and in water not were you washed for cleansing, and rubbed with salt not were you at all, and wrapped not were you at all.
pieces: On the day you were born, no one cut your umbilical cord or washed you with water to clean you. No one rubbed you with salt or wrapped you in cloths.

L.4: And as for your birth, on the day you were born your umbilical cord was not cut, and you were not washed with water to cleanse [you], and you were not rubbed with salt at all, and you were not wrapped in cloths at all.

R.4: On the day you were born, nobody cut the cord that joined you to your mother. Nobody washed you clean with water. Nobody rubbed you with salt or wrapped you in cloths.

decisions.choice: the care a newborn baby was given: cutting the cord, washing, rubbing with salt and wrapping
decisions.reason: These were the first things done for a newborn child. Rubbing the skin with salt was thought to clean and strengthen it, and the baby was wrapped tightly in strips of cloth (compare Luke 2:7). The baby girl in this picture was given none of this care.

decisions.choice: no one cut ... No one rubbed (B); nobody (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs are passive ("was not cut", "were not washed"). Balanced and Readable make them active with "no one", which says the same thing in more natural English and keeps the point that no one cared for her.

records.source: לֹא־חָ֨סָה עָלַ֜יִךְ עַ֗יִן לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֛ךְ אַחַ֥ת מֵאֵ֖לֶּה לְחֻמְלָ֣ה עָלָ֑יִךְ וַֽתֻּשְׁלְכִ֞י אֶל־פְּנֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ בְּגֹ֣עַל נַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ בְּי֖וֹם הֻלֶּ֥דֶת אֹתָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Not looked with pity on you an eye to do for you one of these, to have compassion on you; and you were thrown out onto [the] face of the field in [the] loathing of your life on [the] day you were born.
pieces: No one looked on you with pity or cared enough to do any of these things for you. Instead, you were thrown out on the open ground, because your life was despised on the day you were born.

L.5: No eye pitied you, to do for you any one of these [things], to have compassion on you; and you were thrown out onto the open field, in the loathing of your life, on the day you were born.

R.5: No one felt sorry for you or cared enough to do any of these things for you. On the day you were born, you were thrown out into an open field, because no one wanted you.

decisions.choice: thrown out onto the open field: abandoned and left to die
decisions.reason: In the ancient world an unwanted newborn, often a girl, could be left out in the open to die. The picture is of a baby that no one wanted.

decisions.choice: in the loathing of your life: because your life was despised
decisions.reason: The words "your life" stand for the baby herself (*nefesh*). She was thrown out because she was despised, not by accident.

records.source: וָאֶעֱבֹ֤ר עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ וָֽאֶרְאֵ֔ךְ מִתְבּוֹסֶ֖סֶת בְּדָמָ֑יִךְ וָאֹ֤מַר לָךְ֙ בְּדָמַ֣יִךְ חֲיִ֔י וָאֹ֥מַר לָ֖ךְ בְּדָמַ֥יִךְ חֲיִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I passed by you and I saw you kicking about in your blood, and I said to you, In your blood live! And I said to you, In your blood live!
pieces: Then I passed by you and saw you thrashing about in your blood. There in your blood I said to you, "Live!" There in your blood I said to you, "Live!"

L.6: And I passed by you and saw you kicking about in your blood, and I said to you in your blood, "Live!" And I said to you in your blood, "Live!"

R.6: Then I came by and saw you lying there, kicking about in your blood. And I said to you, "Live!" While you lay there in your blood, I said to you, "Live!"

decisions.choice: in your blood, live: the LORD speaks life to the newborn as she lies unwashed in the blood of her birth
decisions.reason: The blood is the blood of birth that no one washed away (verse 4). The command "Live!" is God's word that keeps her alive. The repetition makes it solemn.

decisions.choice: the sentence is said twice
decisions.reason: The second "and I said to you, in your blood, Live!" repeats the first word for word. The Septuagint and some Hebrew manuscripts have it only once, and it may have been copied twice by mistake. The Hebrew text is followed here, and the repetition reads naturally as emphasis.

decisions.choice: thrashing about (B); kicking about (R)
decisions.reason: The word describes a helpless baby kicking and struggling, not lying still.

records.source: רְבָבָ֗ה כְּצֶ֤מַח הַשָּׂדֶה֙ נְתַתִּ֔יךְ וַתִּרְבִּי֙ וַֽתִּגְדְּלִ֔י וַתָּבֹ֖אִי בַּעֲדִ֣י עֲדָיִ֑ים שָׁדַ֤יִם נָכֹ֨נוּ֙ וּשְׂעָרֵ֣ךְ צִמֵּ֔חַ וְאַ֖תְּ עֵרֹ֥ם וְעֶרְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: [A] ten thousand like [the] growth of the field I made you, and you grew and became great and you came to [the] ornament of ornaments; breasts were formed and your hair had grown, and you [were] naked and bare.
pieces: I made you flourish like a plant in the field. You grew up, became tall and reached the age of full beauty. Your breasts were formed and your hair had grown, but you were still naked and bare.

L.7: I made you thrive like the growth of the field, and you grew and became tall and came to the finest of ornaments; [your] breasts were formed, and your hair had grown; yet you [were] naked and bare.

R.7: I made you grow like a plant in the field. You grew tall and became a beautiful young woman. Your breasts had formed and your hair had grown. But you were still naked, with nothing to wear.

decisions.choice: a ten thousand like the growth of the field I made you: I made you thrive like a plant
alternatives: I made you as many as the plants of the field
decisions.reason: The first word means "ten thousand" or "a great number". It may mean that the LORD made her numerous, but the rest of the verse is about one girl growing up, so it is taken as a picture of growth.

decisions.choice: you came to the ornament of ornaments: you came of age, in the full beauty of a young woman
alternatives: you came to the time of womanhood
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual: "you came to the ornament of ornaments", that is, the finest beauty. Some suggest a slightly different reading, "you came to the time of menstruation", which would also mean that she had reached womanhood. Either way, the next words say what is meant: she was now a grown woman.

decisions.choice: breasts formed, hair grown, naked and bare: she had reached womanhood, but no one had clothed or cared for her
decisions.reason: The signs of puberty show that she was now old enough to be married (verse 8). "Naked and bare" means that she was still poor and uncared for, and it prepares for the covering of verse 8.

decisions.choice: breasts were formed, your hair had grown (every level)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes the signs of puberty in plain words; every level keeps them plainly, without adding to them, as decided at verse 1.

records.source: וָאֶעֱבֹ֨ר עָלַ֜יִךְ וָאֶרְאֵ֗ךְ וְהִנֵּ֤ה עִתֵּךְ֙ עֵ֣ת דֹּדִ֔ים וָאֶפְרֹ֤שׂ כְּנָפִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וָאֲכַסֶּ֖ה עֶרְוָתֵ֑ךְ וָאֶשָּׁ֣בַֽע לָ֠ךְ וָאָב֨וֹא בִבְרִ֜ית אֹתָ֗ךְ נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה וַתִּ֥הְיִי לִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I passed by you and I saw you, and look, your time [was the] time of love; and I spread the skirt of my garment over you and covered your nakedness; and I swore to you and came into a covenant with you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, and you became mine.
pieces: Then I passed by you again and saw you, and you were old enough for love. So I spread the corner of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I gave you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} solemn oath and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, and you became {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

L.8: And I passed by you and saw you, and look, your time [was] the time of love; and I spread the corner of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garment over you and covered your nakedness, and I swore [an oath] to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, and you became {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

R.8: Later I came by again and saw you. You were now old enough for love. So I spread the edge of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} cloak over you and covered your naked body. I made a solemn promise to you and made a marriage covenant with you, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, and you became {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

decisions.choice: your time was the time of love: she was old enough to be married
decisions.reason: "Love" here is the love between husband and wife. The LORD sees that the girl has grown into a woman (verse 7).

decisions.choice: I spread the corner of my garment over you: I took you as my wife
decisions.reason: Spreading the edge of one's garment over a woman was a sign of taking her in marriage and under one's protection (Ruth 3:9; compare Deuteronomy 23:1). It also covers her nakedness, the opposite of the shaming in verse 37.

decisions.choice: the covenant pictured as a marriage: the covenant between the LORD and Israel
decisions.reason: The oath and the covenant are those of a marriage (Malachi 2:14; Proverbs 2:17), and they picture the covenant the LORD made with Israel. Jeremiah 2:2 also speaks of Israel's early days as the love of a bride. "You became mine" is the language of the covenant (Exodus 19:5).

decisions.choice: made a marriage covenant
decisions.reason: Readable adds "marriage" because the picture is of a wedding (m3); the covenant meant is the LORD's covenant with his people.

decisions.choice: gave you my solemn oath (B); made a solemn promise (R)
decisions.reason: "Swore" alone can suggest bad language in modern English; Balanced and Readable say that it was a binding oath.

records.source: וָאֶרְחָצֵ֣ךְ בַּמַּ֔יִם וָאֶשְׁטֹ֥ף דָּמַ֖יִךְ מֵֽעָלָ֑יִךְ וָאֲסֻכֵ֖ךְ בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: And I washed you with water, and I rinsed off your blood from on you, and I anointed you with oil.
pieces: Then I bathed you with water, washed the blood off you and anointed you with oil.

L.9: And I washed you with water and rinsed off your blood from you, and I anointed you with oil.

R.9: Then I bathed you with water and washed the blood off you. I rubbed your skin with oil.

decisions.choice: your blood: blood still on her, which no one had washed away
alternatives: the blood of her monthly period
the blood of the wedding night
decisions.reason: The verse goes back to what was not done for her as a baby (verse 4) and does it now: the LORD washes, anoints and clothes her (verses 9-13). Some take the blood to be that of her monthly period or of the wedding night, but the link with verses 4 and 6 suggests the blood of her birth, still uncleaned.

decisions.choice: anointed you with oil: rubbed with scented oil, as a bride was prepared
decisions.reason: Oil was rubbed into the skin to soothe and perfume it, and a bride was washed and anointed before her wedding (Ruth 3:3; Esther 2:12).

records.source: וָאַלְבִּישֵׁ֣ךְ רִקְמָ֔ה וָאֶנְעֲלֵ֖ךְ תָּ֑חַשׁ וָאֶחְבְּשֵׁ֣ךְ בַּשֵּׁ֔שׁ וַאֲכַסֵּ֖ךְ מֶֽשִׁי׃
records.gloss: And I clothed you [with] embroidered cloth, and I shod you [with] fine leather, and I wound you with fine linen, and I covered you [with] costly fabric.
pieces: I dressed you in embroidered clothing and put sandals of fine leather on your feet. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with costly fabric.

L.10: And I clothed you [with] embroidered cloth and shod you [with] fine leather, and I wound fine linen around you and covered you [with] costly fabric.

R.10: I dressed you in beautiful embroidered clothes and gave you sandals made of the finest leather. I wrapped you in fine linen and gave you expensive clothes to wear.

decisions.choice: fine leather: a costly leather, used in the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The word *tachash* is used for the outer covering of the tabernacle (Exodus 26:14). Its exact meaning is uncertain: it may be a fine, specially treated leather or the skin of a sea animal. Either way it is costly.

decisions.choice: costly fabric: a fine material, perhaps silk
decisions.reason: This word is found only here and in verse 13. It was a luxurious cloth; many take it to be silk, but that is not certain.

decisions.choice: embroidered cloth, fine leather, fine linen: the materials of the tabernacle and of royal and priestly clothing
decisions.reason: The same words are used for the tabernacle's hangings and coverings and the priests' garments (Exodus 26:1, 14, 36; 28:39). Jerusalem is dressed like a queen, and also like the LORD's sanctuary.

records.source: וָאֶעְדֵּ֖ךְ עֶ֑דִי וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה צְמִידִים֙ עַל־יָדַ֔יִךְ וְרָבִ֖יד עַל־גְּרוֹנֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And I adorned you [with] ornaments, and I put bracelets on your hands and a chain on your neck.
pieces: I adorned you with jewelry. I put bracelets on your arms and a necklace around your neck.

L.11: And I adorned you [with] ornaments, and I put bracelets on your hands and a chain on your neck.

R.11: I gave you jewelry to wear. I put bracelets on your arms and a necklace around your neck.

decisions.choice: bracelets and a chain: the jewelry of a bride
decisions.reason: A bride was dressed in her finest jewelry (Isaiah 61:10; Jeremiah 2:32). Abraham's servant gave Rebekah bracelets and a ring as gifts for the bride (Genesis 24:22, 47).

records.source: וָאֶתֵּ֥ן נֶ֨זֶם֙ עַל־אַפֵּ֔ךְ וַעֲגִילִ֖ים עַל־אָזְנָ֑יִךְ וַעֲטֶ֥רֶת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת בְּרֹאשֵֽׁךְ׃
records.gloss: And I put a ring on your nose, and earrings on your ears, and a crown of beauty on your head.
pieces: I put a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears and a beautiful crown on your head.

L.12: And I put a ring on your nose, and earrings on your ears, and a crown of beauty on your head.

R.12: I put a ring in your nose and earrings on your ears. I put a beautiful crown on your head.

decisions.choice: a ring on your nose ... a crown on your head: bridal jewelry and the crown of a queen
decisions.reason: A nose ring was worn by women as jewelry (Genesis 24:47; Isaiah 3:21). The crown shows that she was given royal rank, which verse 13 states.

records.source: וַתַּעְדִּ֞י זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֗סֶף וּמַלְבּוּשֵׁךְ֙ שֵׁ֤שׁ וָמֶ֨שִׁי֙ וְרִקְמָ֔ה סֹ֧לֶת וּדְבַ֛שׁ וָשֶׁ֖מֶן אָכָ֑לְתְּ וַתִּ֨יפִי֙ בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וַֽתִּצְלְחִ֖י לִמְלוּכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And you adorned yourself [with] gold and silver, and your clothing [was] fine linen and costly fabric and embroidered cloth; fine flour and honey and oil you ate; and you were beautiful very very, and you prospered to royalty.
pieces: So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothes were of fine linen, costly fabric and embroidered cloth. You ate the finest flour, honey and olive oil. You became very beautiful indeed, and you rose to be a queen.

L.13: And you adorned yourself with gold and silver, and your clothing [was] fine linen and costly fabric and embroidered cloth; you ate fine flour and honey and oil; and you became very, very beautiful, and you prospered to royalty.

R.13: So you wore gold and silver, and your clothes were made of fine linen, expensive cloth and embroidery. You ate the best flour, with honey and olive oil. You became very beautiful, and you rose to be a queen.

decisions.choice: you prospered to royalty: Jerusalem became a royal city, the seat of David's kingdom
decisions.reason: In the picture the girl becomes a queen. In Israel's history Jerusalem became the capital of David and Solomon's kingdom and the place of the LORD's temple (2 Samuel 5:6-12; 1 Kings 10).

decisions.choice: fine flour, honey and oil: the best food of the land
decisions.reason: These are rich foods, the produce of the land the LORD gave Israel (Deuteronomy 8:8; 32:13-14). Verse 19 says she offered this very food to idols.

decisions.choice: you rose to be a queen
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that she "prospered to royalty", that is, became fit to be a queen. Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨צֵא לָ֥ךְ שֵׁ֛ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם בְּיָפְיֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י׀כָּלִ֣יל ה֗וּא בַּֽהֲדָרִי֙ אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֣מְתִּי עָלַ֔יִךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And went out for you a name among the nations because of your beauty, for it [was] perfect through my splendor which I had put on you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Your fame spread among the nations because of your beauty. It was perfect because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} splendor that I had put on you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: And your name went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it [was] perfect through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} splendor that I had put on you, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: People in other nations heard how beautiful you were. Your beauty was perfect because I had given you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own splendor, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: perfect through my splendor which I had put on you: her beauty was the LORD's gift, not her own
decisions.reason: This sentence prepares for verse 15. Everything she had, from her life to her clothes and her fame, came from the LORD, yet she "trusted in her beauty" as if it were her own. Lamentations 2:15 remembers Jerusalem as "the perfection of beauty".

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.

records.source: וַתִּבְטְחִ֣י בְיָפְיֵ֔ךְ וַתִּזְנִ֖י עַל־שְׁמֵ֑ךְ וַתִּשְׁפְּכִ֧י אֶת־תַּזְנוּתַ֛יִךְ עַל־כָּל־עוֹבֵ֖ר לוֹ־יֶֽהִי׃
records.gloss: And you trusted in your beauty, and you prostituted yourself on account of your name, and you poured out your acts of prostitution on every [one] passing by; his it was.
pieces: But you trusted in your beauty and used your fame to prostitute yourself. You poured out your prostitution on everyone who passed by, and anyone could have you.

L.15: But you trusted in your beauty and prostituted yourself because of your fame, and you poured out your acts of prostitution on every passer-by; it became his.

R.15: But you trusted in your own beauty, and you used your fame to be unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, like a woman with many lovers. You gave yourself to every man who passed by. Anyone could have you.

decisions.choice: you prostituted yourself: Jerusalem turned from the LORD to other gods and other nations, pictured as a wife's promiscuity
decisions.reason: The verb *zanah* means to act as a prostitute. The prophets use it for Israel's unfaithfulness to the LORD: the worship of other gods (verses 16-22) and trust in foreign powers (verses 26-29). Jerusalem in this picture is not a prostitute but a married woman who takes many lovers, and verses 31-34 say that she was worse than a prostitute, because she paid her lovers.

decisions.choice: his it was: she gave her beauty to anyone who wanted it
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words at the end are brief and hard: literally "to him it was" or "let it be his". They seem to say that her beauty became the property of every passer-by. The phrase is short enough that some suspect the text is damaged.

decisions.choice: prostituted yourself (L, B); be unfaithful to me, like a woman with many lovers (R)
decisions.reason: This is the wording set for *zanah* in the published books (Judges 2:17; Jeremiah 3:1). Literal and Balanced keep the picture of prostitution; Readable says what it means, unfaithfulness to the LORD, and keeps the picture of a woman with many lovers. Later verses in this chapter use the shorter "be unfaithful" at Readable.

decisions.choice: anyone could have you (B, R); You gave yourself to every man who passed by (R)
alternatives: You lavished your favors on everyone
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is frank, and Balanced and Readable say plainly what it means without making it cruder (see verse 1).

records.source: וַתִּקְחִ֣י מִבְּגָדַ֗יִךְ וַתַּֽעֲשִׂי־לָךְ֙ בָּמ֣וֹת טְלֻא֔וֹת וַתִּזְנִ֖י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א בָא֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And you took some of your garments, and you made for yourself colorful high places, and you prostituted yourself on them; [such things] not coming and not will be.
pieces: You took some of your clothes and made colorful shrines for yourself on the high places, and there you prostituted yourself. Nothing like this has ever happened, and it never should.

L.16: And you took some of your clothes and made for yourself colorful high places, and you prostituted yourself on them; [such things] have not come, nor will they be.

R.16: You took some of your clothes and used them to decorate hilltop shrines. There you were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with other gods. Nothing like this has ever happened, and it never should.

decisions.choice: colorful high places: shrines for other gods, decorated with cloth
decisions.reason: The high places (*bamot*) were places of worship on hills and raised platforms (see 6:3). She used the clothes the LORD gave her to make couches or hangings for them, as women once wove hangings for the goddess Asherah in the temple (2 Kings 23:7).

decisions.choice: not coming and it will not be: nothing like this has happened or should ever happen
alternatives: they will not come and it will not be
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short and hard: literally "not coming, and it will not be". It is taken as an exclamation that such a thing is unheard of. Some take it as a threat that her shrines will not last.

decisions.choice: unfaithful to me with other gods
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the unfaithfulness was the worship of other gods at the shrines, which is what the picture means (verse 15).

records.source: וַתִּקְחִ֞י כְּלֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֗ךְ מִזְּהָבִ֤י וּמִכַּסְפִּי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ וַתַּעֲשִׂי־לָ֖ךְ צַלְמֵ֣י זָכָ֑ר וַתִּזְנִי־בָֽם׃
records.gloss: And you took your beautiful articles of my gold and of my silver which I had given to you, and you made for yourself images of a male, and you prostituted yourself with them.
pieces: You took your fine jewelry, made of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gold and silver that I had given you, and made yourself male images, and you prostituted yourself with them.

L.17: And you took your beautiful jewelry, [made] of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gold and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} silver that I had given you, and made for yourself images of a male, and you prostituted yourself with them.

R.17: You took the beautiful jewelry I had given you, made of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gold and silver, and you made idols in the shape of men. Then you worshiped them and were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: images of a male: idols in male form
decisions.reason: The phrase means male figures, that is, images of male gods. Some take it to mean images of the male organ, used in fertility worship, but the words do not say so. Either way, worshiping them is pictured as unfaithfulness with lovers.

decisions.choice: my gold and my silver: gifts that belonged to the LORD were turned into idols
decisions.reason: Hosea makes the same charge: Israel used the silver and gold the LORD gave her for Baal (Hosea 2:10).

decisions.choice: Then you worshiped them and were unfaithful to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means, the worship of these images.

records.source: וַתִּקְחִ֛י אֶת־בִּגְדֵ֥י רִקְמָתֵ֖ךְ וַתְּכַסִּ֑ים וְשַׁמְנִי֙ וּקְטָרְתִּ֔י נָתַ֖תְּ לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you took your embroidered garments and covered them, and my oil and my incense you set before them.
pieces: You took your embroidered clothes and dressed them, and you set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oil and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} incense before them.

L.18: And you took your embroidered clothes and covered them, and you set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oil and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} incense before them.

R.18: You dressed the idols in the embroidered clothes I had given you. You offered them the oil and incense that belonged to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: covered them: dressed the idols in clothes
decisions.reason: Idols were dressed in costly clothes as part of their worship (Jeremiah 10:9). Oil and incense were offerings, which belonged to the LORD (Exodus 30:22-38).

decisions.choice: the embroidered clothes I had given you
decisions.reason: Readable adds "I had given you" to link these clothes with verse 10, as the Hebrew "your embroidered clothes" does.

records.source: וְלַחְמִי֩ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֨תִּי לָ֜ךְ סֹ֣לֶת וָשֶׁ֤מֶן וּדְבַשׁ֙ הֶֽאֱכַלְתִּ֔יךְ וּנְתַתִּ֧יהוּ לִפְנֵיהֶ֛ם לְרֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ וַיֶּ֑הִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And my food which I gave to you, fine flour and oil and honey I fed you, and you set it before them for an aroma of soothing; and so it was, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: The food I gave you, the fine flour, oil and honey I fed you with, you set before them as an offering with a pleasing aroma. That is what happened, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.19: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} food that I gave you, fine flour and oil and honey [with which] I fed you, you set it before them as a soothing aroma; and so it was, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.19: I gave you food to eat: the best flour, olive oil and honey. But you offered it to the idols, hoping the smell would please them. That is what you did, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a soothing aroma: the language of sacrifice
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in the Law for offerings that please the LORD (Leviticus 1:9). The food the LORD gave her was offered to idols with the words of his own worship.

decisions.choice: and so it was: it really happened
decisions.reason: The short phrase affirms that this is not exaggeration.

decisions.choice: as an offering with a pleasing aroma
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the wording of the published Leviticus and Genesis 8:21 for this phrase, and adds "an offering" to make the sacrifice plain.

records.source: וַתִּקְחִ֞י אֶת־בָּנַ֤יִךְ וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָלַ֣דְתְּ לִ֔י וַתִּזְבָּחִ֥ים לָהֶ֖ם לֶאֱכ֑וֹל הַמְעַ֖ט מִתַּזְנוּתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And you took your sons and your daughters whom you had borne to me, and you sacrificed them to them to be devoured. [Was it] a small thing [this] from your acts of prostitution,
pieces: You took your sons and daughters, whom you had borne to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and sacrificed them to the idols as food. Was your prostitution not enough,

L.20: And you took your sons and your daughters whom you had borne to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you sacrificed them to them to be devoured. Was your prostitution too small [a thing],

R.20: You took the sons and daughters you had borne to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and sacrificed them to the idols as food. Was it not enough that you were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: whom you had borne to me: the children belonged to the LORD
decisions.reason: In the picture the children are the LORD's own, born of the marriage. Verse 21 calls them "my children". The sin was not only murder but the giving of the LORD's children to other gods.

decisions.choice: sacrificed them to be devoured: child sacrifice to other gods
decisions.reason: Kings of Judah such as Ahaz and Manasseh offered their children in fire (2 Kings 16:3; 21:6), and Jeremiah condemns it (Jeremiah 7:31; 19:5). The Law forbade it (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31). "To be devoured" pictures the children as food for the idols.

decisions.choice: to the idols
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to the male images of verse 17; Balanced and Readable name them.

records.source: וַֽתִּשְׁחֲטִ֖י אֶת־בָּנָ֑י וַֽתִּתְּנִ֔ים בְּהַעֲבִ֥יר אוֹתָ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: that you slaughtered my children and gave them, making them pass through to them?
pieces: that you slaughtered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} children and gave them up to the idols, making them pass through the fire?

L.21: that you slaughtered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} children and gave them up, making them pass through [the fire] to them?

R.21: You even slaughtered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} children and gave them to the idols, burning them in the fire.

decisions.choice: making them pass through to them: burning them as offerings
decisions.reason: "Make pass through" is short for "make pass through the fire" (2 Kings 16:3; 23:10), the burning of children as offerings.

decisions.choice: the fire (B); burning them in the fire (R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "the fire", which the Hebrew implies; Balanced and Readable state it. Readable ends the question of verse 20 there and makes this a statement.

records.source: וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־תּוֹעֲבֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ וְתַזְנֻתַ֔יִךְ לֹ֥א זָכַ֖רְתְּ אֶת־יְמֵ֣י נְעוּרָ֑יִךְ בִּֽהְיוֹתֵךְ֙ עֵרֹ֣ם וְעֶרְיָ֔ה מִתְבּוֹסֶ֥סֶת בְּדָמֵ֖ךְ הָיִֽית׃
records.gloss: And in all your abominations and your acts of prostitution not you remembered the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood you were.
pieces: In all your detestable practices and your prostitution, you never once remembered your early days, when you were naked and bare, thrashing about in your blood.

L.22: And in all your abominations and your prostitution you did not call to mind the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.

R.22: While you were doing all these disgusting things and being unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you never remembered how you were when you were young. Back then you were naked, with nothing to wear, kicking about in your own blood.

decisions.choice: you did not remember the days of your youth: she forgot that she owed everything to the LORD
decisions.reason: To "remember" in the Bible is to keep in mind and act on it (Deuteronomy 8:2, 18). Verse 60 answers this: the LORD will remember his covenant made in her youth, even though she did not.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י אַחֲרֵ֖י כָּל־רָעָתֵ֑ךְ א֣וֹי א֣וֹי לָ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was after all your wickedness, woe, woe to you! declares [the] Lord Yahweh,
pieces: After all your wickedness (woe, woe to you! declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}),

L.23: And it came about after all your wickedness (woe, woe to you! declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}),

R.23: After you had done all these evil things (how terrible, how terrible it will be for you! says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}),

decisions.choice: after all your wickedness: the sentence continues in verse 24, and the cry of woe breaks into it
decisions.reason: The verse begins a sentence that runs on into verse 24 ("you built yourself a mound"). The cry "woe, woe to you" interrupts it, as if the speaker cannot go on without crying out.

decisions.choice: woe, woe to you (L, B); how terrible, how terrible it will be for you (R)
decisions.reason: The cry *'oy* aimed at others follows the wording set for Isaiah's *hoy*. The Hebrew says it twice, and every level keeps both.

records.source: וַתִּבְנִי־לָ֖ךְ גֶּ֑בוַתַּעֲשִׂי־לָ֥ךְ רָמָ֖ה בְּכָל־רְחֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: you built for yourself a mound and made for yourself a lofty place in every square.
pieces: you built yourself a platform and made yourself a lofty shrine in every public square.

L.24: that you built for yourself a mound and made for yourself a lofty place in every square.

R.24: you built yourself a platform for worship and made yourself a shrine in every town square.

decisions.choice: a mound ... a lofty place: raised platforms for the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: The first word means something curved or raised, such as a mound, a platform or a vaulted room; the second means a high place. Both seem to be shrines built in the city's squares, the town's version of the high places on the hills (verse 16). The Septuagint understood the first word as a house of prostitution.

decisions.choice: platform (B, R); lofty shrine (B); shrine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use words that name what these were, places of worship, without choosing among the more specific meanings (m1).

records.source: אֶל־כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ דֶּ֗רֶךְ בָּנִית֙ רָֽמָתֵ֔ךְ וַתְּתַֽעֲבִי֙ אֶת־יָפְיֵ֔ךְ וַתְּפַשְּׂקִ֥י אֶת־רַגְלַ֖יִךְ לְכָל־עוֹבֵ֑ר וַתַּרְבִּ֖י אֶת־תַּזְנוּתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: At every head of a road you built your lofty place, and you made your beauty abominable, and you spread your feet to every [one] passing by, and you multiplied your acts of prostitution.
pieces: At the head of every street you built your lofty shrine and made your beauty something detestable. You spread your legs for everyone who passed by and multiplied your prostitution.

L.25: At the head of every road you built your lofty place and made your beauty an abomination; and you spread your feet to everyone passing by and multiplied your prostitution.

R.25: You built a shrine at every street corner, and you made your beauty something disgusting. You offered your body to every man who passed by, and you were more and more unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: you spread your feet: you offered yourself sexually
decisions.reason: "Feet" is a polite word here for the legs, as it sometimes is in Hebrew (compare Isaiah 7:20). The picture is of a woman offering herself to any man.

decisions.choice: you made your beauty abominable: the beauty the LORD gave her became something disgusting
decisions.reason: The verb is related to *to'evah*. Her beauty, which was the LORD's gift (verse 14), was turned into something he finds repulsive.

decisions.choice: spread your legs (B); offered your body (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "feet". Balanced says plainly what the gesture means, and Readable gives its meaning in sober words. Neither makes it cruder than the Hebrew or hides it (see verse 1).

records.source: וַתִּזְנִ֧י אֶל־בְּנֵֽי־מִצְרַ֛יִם שְׁכֵנַ֖יִךְ גִּדְלֵ֣י בָשָׂ֑ר וַתַּרְבִּ֥י אֶת־תַּזְנֻתֵ֖ךְ לְהַכְעִיסֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And you prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors, great of flesh; and you multiplied your prostitution to provoke me to anger.
pieces: You prostituted yourself with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, and you multiplied your prostitution to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger.

L.26: And you prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great of flesh, and you multiplied your prostitution to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger.

R.26: You were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with the Egyptians, your neighbors who were full of lust. You were unfaithful again and again, and so you made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry.

decisions.choice: the sons of Egypt: Judah's alliances with Egypt and its gods
decisions.reason: The kings of Judah more than once looked to Egypt for help against Assyria and Babylon, and the prophets condemned it as a lack of trust in the LORD (Isaiah 30:1-5; 31:1; Jeremiah 2:18, 36). Such treaties also brought in the worship of the other nation's gods.

decisions.choice: great of flesh: sexually potent
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means the male body, as in 23:20 and Leviticus 15:2. The phrase pictures Egypt as a lover who attracted her by his strength.

decisions.choice: your lustful neighbors (B); who were full of lust (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase. Balanced and Readable state its point, Egypt's strong desire and attraction, without spelling out the body part (see verse 1).

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֨ה נָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וָאֶגְרַ֖ע חֻקֵּ֑ךְ וָאֶתְּנֵ֞ךְ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ שֹׂנְאוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים הַנִּכְלָמ֖וֹת מִדַּרְכֵּ֥ךְ זִמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And look, I stretched out my hand against you and I diminished your allotment, and I gave you to [the] desire of those who hate you, the daughters of [the] Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
pieces: So I stretched out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and cut down your allotted portion. I handed you over to the will of those who hate you, the Philistine cities, who were shocked by your lewd behavior.

L.27: And look, I stretched out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and diminished your allotted portion, and I gave you to the desire of those hating you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed because of your lewd way.

R.27: So I used {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against you and gave you less than before. I let your enemies, the Philistine towns, do what they wanted with you. Even they were shocked by your shameful ways.

decisions.choice: I diminished your allotment: I reduced what was due to her
decisions.reason: The word means a fixed share, such as the food and clothing a husband owed his wife (Exodus 21:10). In history it may refer to the loss of land and towns to Judah's enemies.

decisions.choice: the daughters of the Philistines: the Philistine cities
decisions.reason: "Daughters" can mean the towns of a people (as verse 46). The Philistines took towns from Judah in the reign of Ahaz (2 Chronicles 28:18), and after the Assyrian invasion of 701 BC towns of Judah were given to Philistine kings. Even these pagan neighbors were ashamed of Jerusalem's behavior.

decisions.choice: lewd conduct: shameful, wicked behavior, here sexual
decisions.reason: The word *zimmah* is used for sexual sin (Leviticus 18:17) and for wicked plans in general. Here it continues the picture of the unfaithful wife.

decisions.choice: the Philistine cities (B); the Philistine towns (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "daughters" means here (m2), and Balanced says "shocked by" for "ashamed of", the sense of the Hebrew here.

records.source: וַתִּזְנִי֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר מִבִּלְתִּ֖י שָׂבְעָתֵ֑ךְ וַתִּזְנִ֕ים וְגַ֖ם לֹ֥א שָׂבָֽעַתְּ׃
records.gloss: And you prostituted yourself with the sons of Assyria, from not your being satisfied; and you prostituted yourself with them, and also you were not satisfied.
pieces: You prostituted yourself with the Assyrians too, because you could not be satisfied. You prostituted yourself with them, and even then you were not satisfied.

L.28: And you prostituted yourself with the sons of Assyria, because you were not satisfied; and you prostituted yourself with them, and still you were not satisfied.

R.28: You were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with the Assyrians too, because you were never satisfied. You went to them, and still you were not satisfied.

decisions.choice: the sons of Assyria: Judah's dealings with Assyria
decisions.reason: King Ahaz sought Assyria's help, paid it tribute and copied an altar he saw in Damascus (2 Kings 16:7-18). Hosea 8:9 uses the same picture of Israel hiring lovers in Assyria.

decisions.choice: the Assyrians (B, R)
decisions.reason: "The sons of" a nation means its people; Balanced and Readable use the plain name.

records.source: וַתַּרְבִּ֧י אֶת־תַּזְנוּתֵ֛ךְ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנַ֖עַן כַּשְׂדִּ֑ימָה וְגַם־בְּזֹ֖את לֹ֥א שָׂבָֽעַתְּ׃
records.gloss: And you multiplied your prostitution to [the] land of merchants, to Chaldea; and also with this you were not satisfied.
pieces: You multiplied your prostitution with Chaldea, the land of traders, and even this did not satisfy you.

L.29: And you multiplied your prostitution with the land of merchants, Chaldea; and even with this you were not satisfied.

R.29: Then you were unfaithful with the Babylonians too, a nation of traders. But even that did not satisfy you.

decisions.choice: land of merchants: the word Canaan, used for "traders"
decisions.reason: The word for merchants is *kena'an*, the name Canaan, whose people were known as traders (Hosea 12:8; Zephaniah 1:11). Here it describes Babylonia, as in 17:4.

decisions.choice: Chaldea: Babylonia
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans ruled Babylon in Ezekiel's day. Judah's kings sought Babylon's favor (2 Kings 20:12-19) and later rebelled against it (2 Kings 24:1, 20).

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: Readable names the Chaldeans as Babylonians, the wording set for the prophets.

records.source: מָ֤ה אֲמֻלָה֙ לִבָּתֵ֔ךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה בַּעֲשׂוֹתֵךְ֙ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֔לֶּה מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אִשָּֽׁה־זוֹנָ֖ה שַׁלָּֽטֶת׃
records.gloss: How sick [is] your heart, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, in your doing all these [things], [the] deeds of a woman, a domineering prostitute,
pieces: How sick your heart is, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, that you do all these things, the deeds of a shameless prostitute,

L.30: How sick [is] your heart, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, in your doing all these [things], the deeds of a brazen prostitute woman,

R.30: Your heart is so sick, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! You do all these things, just like a shameless prostitute.

decisions.choice: how sick is your heart: how weak and sick with desire she is
alternatives: how I am filled with anger against you
decisions.reason: The word for "sick" or "weak" is rare, and the form of "heart" is found only here. Some read the phrase as "how I am filled with fury against you", using a similar word in a related language. The usual reading, a heart sick or weak with longing, fits the picture of a woman who cannot stop.

decisions.choice: a domineering prostitute: a shameless prostitute who does as she likes
decisions.reason: The second word means ruling or domineering. She acts without restraint or shame.

decisions.choice: just like a shameless prostitute
alternatives: the deeds of a brazen prostitute woman
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew compares her to an actual prostitute, so Readable says "prostitute" plainly, as the settled note allows where prostitution itself is meant.

records.source: בִּבְנוֹתַ֤יִךְ גַּבֵּךְ֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ כָּל־דֶּ֔רֶךְ וְרָמָתֵ֥ךְ עָשִׂ֖ית בְּכָל־רְח֑וֹב וְלֹא־הָיִ֥ית כַּזּוֹנָ֖ה לְקַלֵּ֥ס אֶתְנָֽן׃

pieces: building your platform at the head of every street and making your lofty shrine in every public square! Yet you were not like a prostitute, because you scorned payment.

L.31: in your building your mound at the head of every road and making your lofty place in every square! Yet you were not like a prostitute, for you scorned payment.

R.31: You built your platforms at every street corner and your shrines in every town square. But you were not like a prostitute, because you refused to be paid.

decisions.choice: you were not like a prostitute, scorning payment: she was worse, because she did not even take payment
alternatives: you were not like a prostitute who scorns payment to raise her price
decisions.reason: She did not do it for money, as a prostitute does; verses 33-34 explain that she paid her lovers instead.

records.source: הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַמְּנָאָ֑פֶת תַּ֣חַת אִישָׁ֔הּ תִּקַּ֖ח אֶת־זָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: The wife, the adulterous, instead of her husband she takes strangers.
pieces: You adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!

L.32: The adulterous wife! Instead of her husband she takes strangers.

R.32: You are a wife who commits adultery. You take other men instead of your own husband.

decisions.choice: the adulterous wife: the picture is named plainly, a married woman who is unfaithful
decisions.reason: Here the chapter says outright what it has pictured: Jerusalem is a wife who has broken her marriage. The Law made adultery a capital crime (Leviticus 20:10), which is the background of verses 38-40.

decisions.choice: You are a wife who commits adultery
decisions.reason: Readable makes the exclamation a statement addressed to her, and says "other men" for "strangers".

records.source: לְכָל־זֹנ֖וֹת יִתְּנוּ־נֵ֑דֶה וְאַ֨תְּ נָתַ֤תְּ אֶת־נְדָנַ֨יִךְ֙ לְכָל־מְאַֽהֲבַ֔יִךְ וַתִּשְׁחֳדִ֣י אוֹתָ֗ם לָב֥וֹא אֵלַ֛יִךְ מִסָּבִ֖יב בְּתַזְנוּתָֽיִךְ׃
