pieces: All prostitutes are given gifts, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers. You paid them bribes so that they would come from every side for your prostitution.

L.33: To all prostitutes [men] give a gift, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, and you bribed them to come to you from all around for your prostitution.

R.33: Men pay prostitutes. But you paid all your lovers! You paid them bribes so that they would come from everywhere and you could be unfaithful with them.

decisions.choice: you gave your gifts to all your lovers: Judah paid tribute to foreign powers
decisions.reason: The picture fits the tribute that Judah's kings sent to Assyria and others to buy their help (2 Kings 16:8; 18:14-16). Hosea 8:9-10 also says that Israel "hired lovers".

records.source: וַיְהִי־בָ֨ךְ הֵ֤פֶךְ מִן־הַנָּשִׁים֙ בְּתַזְנוּתַ֔יִךְ וְאַחֲרַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א זוּנָּ֑ה וּבְתִתֵּ֣ךְ אֶתְנָ֗ן וְאֶתְנַ֛ן לֹ֥א נִתַּן־לָ֖ךְ וַתְּהִ֥י לְהֶֽפֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And there was in you [the] opposite from [other] women in your acts of prostitution, and after you no one was solicited for prostitution; and in your giving payment, and payment not was given to you, you became the opposite.
pieces: So in your prostitution you were the opposite of other women. No one came after you to hire you; you paid, and no one paid you. You were the opposite.

L.34: So in your prostitution you were the opposite of [other] women: no one solicited you for prostitution, and you gave payment and no payment was given to you; so you were the opposite.

R.34: So you were not like other women who are prostitutes. No one came looking for you. You paid them, and they did not pay you. You did the opposite of what prostitutes do.

decisions.choice: the opposite: the word begins and ends the verse
decisions.reason: The word for "opposite" frames the verse. Everything about her prostitution was the reverse of the normal trade: she sought her lovers and paid them.

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן זוֹנָ֔ה שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Therefore, prostitute, hear [the] word of Yahweh.
pieces: Therefore, you prostitute, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.35: Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.35: So, you prostitute, listen to the message of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!

decisions.choice: therefore: the sentence of judgment begins
decisions.reason: The charges have been laid (verses 15-34). From here the LORD announces the punishment (verses 35-43).

decisions.choice: you prostitute (every level)
decisions.reason: She is addressed by the insult she has earned (verses 30-34), so Readable keeps the word, as the settled note allows where the comparison is with prostitution itself.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה יַ֣עַן הִשָּׁפֵ֤ךְ נְחֻשְׁתֵּךְ֙ וַתִּגָּלֶ֣ה עֶרְוָתֵ֔ךְ בְּתַזְנוּתַ֖יִךְ עַל־מְאַהֲבָ֑יִךְ וְעַל֙ כָּל־גִּלּוּלֵ֣י תוֹעֲבוֹתַ֔יִךְ וְכִדְמֵ֣י בָנַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תְּ לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness uncovered in your acts of prostitution with your lovers, and with all the idols of your abominations, and according to [the] blood of your children whom you gave to them,
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Because you poured out your lust and exposed your nakedness as you prostituted yourself with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because you gave them the blood of your children,

L.36: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness was uncovered in your prostitution with your lovers and with all the filthy idols of your abominations, and because of the blood of your children whom you gave to them,

R.36: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You poured out your lust and showed your naked body to your lovers when you were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You worshiped all your disgusting idols. You gave them the blood of your children.

decisions.choice: your lust: her desire, poured out freely
alternatives: your copper, that is, your money
decisions.reason: The usual word with these letters means copper or bronze, and some take it to mean the money she spent on her lovers (verses 33-34). Others take it to be a related word for lust or for a bodily discharge. The context of nakedness and lovers suggests lust.

decisions.choice: the idols of your abominations: idols that are hateful to the LORD
decisions.reason: The word for idols is *gillulim* (see 6:4), set beside *to'evah*.

decisions.choice: the filthy idols of your abominations (L); your detestable idols (B); your disgusting idols (R)
decisions.reason: *Gillulim* follows the settled wording, "filthy idols" (Literal) and "idols" (Balanced, Readable). Balanced and Readable fold *to'evah* into one adjective, using its settled words.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula.

records.heading: The sentence on the unfaithful wife

records.source: לָ֠כֵן הִנְנִ֨י מְקַבֵּ֤ץ אֶת־כָּל־מְאַהֲבַ֨יִךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָרַ֣בְתְּ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֵת֙ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהַ֔בְתְּ עַ֖ל כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׂנֵ֑את וְקִבַּצְתִּי֩ אֹתָ֨ם עָלַ֜יִךְ מִסָּבִ֗יב וְגִלֵּיתִ֤י עֶרְוָתֵךְ֙ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וְרָא֖וּ אֶת־כָּל־עֶרְוָתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: therefore, look, I am gathering all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, and all whom you loved along with all whom you hated; and I will gather them against you from all around, and I will uncover your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.
pieces: therefore I am about to gather all your lovers whom you pleased, everyone you loved and everyone you hated. I will bring them against you from all around and strip you naked in front of them, and they will see all your nakedness.

L.37: therefore look, I am gathering all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, and all whom you loved along with all whom you hated; and I will gather them against you from all around and uncover your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.

R.37: So I am going to gather all your lovers, the ones you pleased, both those you loved and those you hated. I will bring them against you from every side. I will strip you naked in front of them, and they will see you completely naked.

decisions.choice: I will uncover your nakedness to them: the public shaming of an adulterous wife
decisions.reason: Stripping was a punishment of public shame for an unfaithful wife (Hosea 2:5, 12; Jeremiah 13:26). It reverses verse 8, where the LORD covered her nakedness.

decisions.choice: the lovers become the attackers: the nations she courted will destroy the city
decisions.reason: The picture stands for history: the nations Jerusalem relied on and copied will come against her, and Babylon will besiege and destroy the city. The language of a husband punishing his wife is a picture of the LORD's judgment on a city; it describes what happened to Jerusalem, and it is not a pattern for how anyone is to be treated.

decisions.choice: strip you naked (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what "uncover your nakedness" means here, without adding to it (see verse 1).

records.source: וּשְׁפַטְתִּיךְ֙ מִשְׁפְּטֵ֣י נֹאֲפ֔וֹת וְשֹׁפְכֹ֖ת דָּ֑ם וּנְתַתִּ֕יךְ דַּ֥ם חֵמָ֖ה וְקִנְאָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will judge you [with the] judgments of adulteresses and [of women who] shed blood, and I will give you [the] blood of wrath and jealousy.
pieces: I will sentence you as women who commit adultery and murder are sentenced, and I will bring on you the bloodshed of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath and jealousy.

L.38: And I will judge you [with] the judgments of adulteresses and of women who shed blood, and I will give you the blood of wrath and jealousy.

R.38: I will punish you as women are punished for adultery and murder. In {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and jealousy I will put you to death.

decisions.choice: the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood: the penalties of the Law
decisions.reason: Adultery and murder were both punished by death under the Law (Leviticus 20:10; Genesis 9:6). Jerusalem was guilty of both: of unfaithfulness and of the blood of her children (verse 36).

decisions.choice: jealousy: the LORD's zeal for a covenant that is his alone
decisions.reason: The word means the passion of a husband who will not share his wife, and it is used of the LORD, who will not share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14).

decisions.choice: I will put you to death
alternatives: I will bring on you the blood of wrath
decisions.reason: "Bring blood on" someone means to put them to death. Readable says so plainly.

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֨י אוֹתָ֜ךְ בְּיָדָ֗ם וְהָרְס֤וּ גַבֵּךְ֙ וְנִתְּצ֣וּ רָמֹתַ֔יִךְ וְהִפְשִׁ֤יטוּ אוֹתָךְ֙ בְּגָדַ֔יִךְ וְלָקְח֖וּ כְּלֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֑ךְ וְהִנִּיח֖וּךְ עֵירֹ֥ם וְעֶרְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will give you into their hand, and they will tear down your mound and break down your lofty places, and they will strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewelry, and they will leave you naked and bare.
pieces: I will hand you over to them, and they will tear down your platform and demolish your lofty shrines. They will strip you of your clothes and take away your fine jewelry, leaving you naked and bare.

L.39: And I will give you into their hand, and they will tear down your mound and break down your lofty places; and they will strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewelry and leave you naked and bare.

R.39: I will hand you over to your lovers. They will tear down your platforms and destroy your shrines. They will strip off your clothes and take your beautiful jewelry. They will leave you naked, with nothing.

decisions.choice: naked and bare: she ends as she began
decisions.reason: The same words describe her as a girl before the LORD clothed her (verses 7 and 22). All his gifts are taken away.

decisions.choice: your lovers
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are, the lovers of verse 37.

records.source: וְהֶעֱל֤וּ עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ קָהָ֔ל וְרָגְמ֥וּ אוֹתָ֖ךְ בָּאָ֑בֶן וּבִתְּק֖וּךְ בְּחַרְבוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And they will bring up against you an assembly, and they will stone you with stones and cut you to pieces with their swords.
pieces: They will bring up a mob against you, and they will stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords.

L.40: And they will bring up an assembly against you, and they will stone you with stones and cut you to pieces with their swords.

R.40: They will bring a crowd against you. They will throw stones at you and cut you to pieces with their swords.

decisions.choice: an assembly ... stone you: the punishment for adultery carried out by the community
decisions.reason: Under the Law the people of the town stoned an adulteress (Deuteronomy 22:21-24). The swords belong to an army; the picture of an execution merges with the city's fall to its enemies.

records.source: וְשָׂרְפ֤וּ בָתַּ֨יִךְ֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעָשׂוּ־בָ֣ךְ שְׁפָטִ֔ים לְעֵינֵ֖י נָשִׁ֣ים רַבּ֑וֹת וְהִשְׁבַּתִּיךְ֙ מִזּוֹנָ֔ה וְגַם־אֶתְנַ֖ן לֹ֥א תִתְּנִי־עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And they will burn your houses with fire and execute on you judgments before [the] eyes of many women; and I will make you stop from [being] a prostitute, and also payment you will not give again.
pieces: They will burn down your houses and carry out judgments on you while many women look on. I will stop your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers.

L.41: And they will burn your houses with fire and carry out judgments on you in the sight of many women; and I will make you stop being a prostitute, and you will no longer give payment.

R.41: They will burn down your houses and punish you while many women watch. I will put a stop to your unfaithfulness, and you will not pay lovers anymore.

decisions.choice: they will burn your houses: the burning of Jerusalem by the Babylonians
decisions.reason: When the city fell in 586 BC, the Babylonians burned the temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:9).

decisions.choice: in the sight of many women: in front of the other nations
decisions.reason: The "many women" are the other cities and nations, who will see her punishment as a warning (compare 23:48).

records.source: וַהֲנִחֹתִ֤י חֲמָתִי֙ בָּ֔ךְ וְסָ֥רָה קִנְאָתִ֖י מִמֵּ֑ךְ וְשָׁ֣קַטְתִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א אֶכְעַ֖ס עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And I will bring to rest my wrath on you, and my jealousy will turn away from you, and I will be quiet and not be angry again.
pieces: Then I will satisfy {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy will turn away from you. I will be calm and no longer angry.

L.42: And I will bring {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you to rest, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy will turn away from you; and I will be calm and will not be angry anymore.

R.42: Then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against you will be finished, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy will leave you. I will be calm and will not be angry anymore.

decisions.choice: I will bring my wrath to rest: the LORD's anger will be fully spent
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in 5:13 and 21:22. The anger ends because the judgment has been carried out. Whether this is also a hint of mercy is not said; verses 59-63 go on to the promise.

records.source: יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־זָכַרְתְּ֙ אֶת־יְמֵ֣י נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ וַתִּרְגְּזִי־לִ֖י בְּכָל־אֵ֑לֶּה וְגַם־אֲנִ֨י הֵ֜א דַּרְכֵּ֣ךְ׀בְּרֹ֣אשׁ נָתַ֗תִּי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְלֹ֤א עָשִׂית֙ אֶת־הַזִּמָּ֔ה עַ֖ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲבֹתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: Because that not you remembered the days of your youth, and you raged at me in all these, and also I, look, your way on [your] head I have given, declares [the] Lord Yahweh; and not have you done the lewdness on all your abominations?
pieces: Since you forgot the days of your youth and provoked {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all these things, I in turn will bring your deeds down on your own head, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Did you not add lewdness to all your other detestable practices?

L.43: Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but raged against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in all these [things], look, I also have brought your way on [your] head, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. And have you not committed this lewdness on top of all your abominations?

R.43: You did not remember what it was like when you were young. You made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry with all these things. So I will make you pay for what you have done, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. You added shameful immorality to all your other disgusting practices.

decisions.choice: I have given your way on your head: I will make you bear the results of your conduct
decisions.reason: To bring someone's way on their head means to repay them for what they have done (9:10; 11:21).

decisions.choice: have you not committed this lewdness: a question expecting "yes"
alternatives: and you will not commit lewdness again
did I not deal with your lewdness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can be read as "I have not done" or "you have not done", and as a question or a statement. Read as a question with "you", it is a final charge: she added sexual sin to her other abominations. Others read a promise that she will not do it again.

decisions.choice: shameful immorality
decisions.reason: "Lewdness" is not common in everyday English. Readable says what it means here.

records.source: הִנֵּה֙ כָּל־הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל עָלַ֥יִךְ יִמְשֹׁ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר כְּאִמָּ֖ה בִּתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Look, every one who speaks proverbs will speak a proverb about you, saying, Like [the] mother, her daughter.
pieces: Everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this one about you: "Like mother, like daughter."

L.44: Look, everyone who uses proverbs will use [this] proverb about you, saying, "Like mother, like her daughter."

R.44: People who like to quote sayings will say this about you: "The daughter is just like her mother."

decisions.choice: like mother, her daughter: a child shows the character of the parent
decisions.reason: The proverb is three words in Hebrew. Verse 45 explains it: Jerusalem's "mother" was a Hittite (verse 3), and Jerusalem behaves like her.

records.source: בַּת־אִמֵּ֣ךְ אַ֔תְּ גֹּעֶ֥לֶת אִישָׁ֖הּ וּבָנֶ֑יהָ וַאֲח֨וֹת אֲחוֹתֵ֜ךְ אַ֗תְּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר גָּֽעֲ֨לוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁיהֶ֣ן וּבְנֵיהֶ֔ן אִמְּכֶ֣ן חִתִּ֔ית וַאֲבִיכֶ֖ן אֱמֹרִֽי׃
records.gloss: Your mother's daughter [are] you, who loathed her husband and her children; and your sisters' sister [are] you, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother [was] a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
pieces: You are truly your mother's daughter, who despised her husband and her children. And you are truly the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and their children. The mother of you all was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.

L.45: Your mother's daughter [are] you, who loathed her husband and her children; and your sisters' sister [are] you, who loathed their husbands and their children. The mother of [you all was] a Hittite, and the father of [you all] an Amorite.

R.45: You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her children. You are just like your sisters, who hated their husbands and their children. All of you had a Hittite mother and an Amorite father.

decisions.choice: who loathed her husband and her children: the family likeness is unfaithfulness and the killing of children
decisions.reason: The picture is of a family who all despise their husbands and children. For Jerusalem it means turning from the LORD and sacrificing her children (verses 20-21). The text does not say who the "husbands" of the mother and sisters are; the point is the likeness.

decisions.choice: your mother a Hittite and your father an Amorite: verse 3 again, now said to all three sisters
decisions.reason: The parents of verse 3 are named again, in the opposite order, to close the comparison. Here "your" is plural: Jerusalem, Samaria and Sodom share the same parents.

decisions.choice: the mother of you all (L, B); All of you had (R)
decisions.reason: The plural "your" is shown in English, which cannot mark it on the word itself, so that the reader sees that the sisters of verse 46 are included.

records.source: וַאֲחוֹתֵ֨ךְ הַגְּדוֹלָ֤ה שֹֽׁמְרוֹן֙ הִ֣יא וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת עַל־שְׂמֹאולֵ֑ךְ וַאֲחוֹתֵ֞ךְ הַקְּטַנָּ֣ה מִמֵּ֗ךְ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֨בֶת֙ מִֽימִינֵ֔ךְ סְדֹ֖ם וּבְנוֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And your sister, the big one, [is] Samaria, she and her daughters, who dwell at your left; and your sister, the small one more than you, who dwells at your right, [is] Sodom and her daughters.
pieces: Your older sister is Samaria, who lived with her daughters to the north of you, and your younger sister, who lived with her daughters to the south of you, is Sodom.

L.46: And your older sister [is] Samaria, she and her daughters, who live at your left; and your sister younger than you, who lives at your right, [is] Sodom and her daughters.

R.46: Your older sister is Samaria, who lived with her towns to the north of you. Your younger sister is Sodom, who lived with her towns to the south of you.

decisions.choice: at your left ... at your right: to the north and to the south
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "at your left" and "at your right". A person facing east, as the Hebrew way of giving directions does, has the north on the left and the south on the right. Samaria lay north of Jerusalem and Sodom to the south, by the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the big one ... the small one: older and younger, or greater and lesser
decisions.reason: The words mean "big" and "small". They are usually taken as older and younger sister, but they may also mean the larger and smaller city.

decisions.choice: her daughters: the towns around a city
decisions.reason: A city's "daughters" are the smaller towns that belong to it (Numbers 21:25).

decisions.choice: her towns
decisions.reason: Readable says what "daughters" means here (m3). Literal and Balanced keep the family picture, which the chapter builds on.

decisions.choice: to the north of you ... to the south of you
alternatives: at your left ... at your right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the directions as English states them (m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew.

records.source: וְלֹ֤א בְדַרְכֵיהֶן֙ הָלַ֔כְתְּ וּבְתוֹעֲבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֖ן עָשִׂ֑ית כִּמְעַ֣ט קָ֔ט וַתַּשְׁחִ֥תִי מֵהֵ֖ן בְּכָל־דְּרָכָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And not in their ways did you walk, and according to their abominations did you do, as a little, only; and you acted more corruptly than they in all your ways.
pieces: You did not just walk in their ways and copy their detestable practices. As if that were not enough, you became more corrupt than they were in all your ways.

L.47: And you did not walk in their ways and do according to their abominations [only]; as if that were too little, you acted more corruptly than they in all your ways.

R.47: You did not just live the way they did and copy their disgusting practices. That was not enough for you. You became even more evil than they were in everything you did.

decisions.choice: as a little, only: as if that were too small a thing
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "very soon" or "as if it were a little thing". Here it is taken in the second sense, which fits the comparison: copying her sisters was not enough for her.

records.source: חַי־אָ֗נִי נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אִם־עָֽשְׂתָה֙ סְדֹ֣ם אֲחוֹתֵ֔ךְ הִ֖יא וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית אַ֖תְּ וּבְנוֹתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, not has done Sodom your sister, she and her daughters, as you have done, you and your daughters.
pieces: As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, not even your sister Sodom and her daughters did what you and your daughters have done.

L.48: [As] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, Sodom your sister, she and her daughters, has not done as you have done, you and your daughters.

R.48: As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, your sister Sodom and her towns never did the evil things that you and your towns have done.

decisions.choice: as I live: the LORD's oath by his own life
decisions.reason: The LORD swears by his own life, the strongest oath there is (Numbers 14:21; Isaiah 49:18).

decisions.choice: As I live, declares the Lord GOD (L); As surely as I live (B, R)
decisions.reason: The oath follows the wording used in Isaiah 49:18 and Jeremiah 22:24.

records.source: הִנֵּה־זֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה עֲוֺ֖ן סְדֹ֣ם אֲחוֹתֵ֑ךְ גָּא֨וֹן שִׂבְעַת־לֶ֜חֶם וְשַׁלְוַ֣ת הַשְׁקֵ֗ט הָ֤יָה לָהּ֙ וְלִבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְיַד־עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְי֖וֹן לֹ֥א הֶחֱזִֽיקָה׃
records.gloss: Look, this was [the] iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, abundance of bread, and ease of quiet belonged to her and to her daughters, and [the] hand of [the] poor and needy not she strengthened.
pieces: This was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, more food than they needed and careless ease, but they did not help the poor and needy.

L.49: Look, this was the iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, abundance of food and careless ease belonged to her and to her daughters, but she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

R.49: This was the sin of your sister Sodom: She and her towns were proud. They had more than enough to eat and lived in comfort without a care. But they did not help poor people and those in need.

decisions.choice: the sin of Sodom: pride, excess and the neglect of the poor
decisions.reason: Ezekiel names sins that Jerusalem shared: pride, plenty and indifference to the needy. Verse 50 adds that they did "an abomination". Genesis 18-19 tells of the outcry against Sodom and of the violence its men offered to strangers (Genesis 19:4-9). Ezekiel's list does not replace that account; it shows that Sodom's guilt included the neglect of the poor.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sin (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'awon*.

records.source: וַֽתִּגְבְּהֶ֔ינָה וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֥ינָה תוֹעֵבָ֖ה לְפָנָ֑י וָאָסִ֥יר אֶתְהֶ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִֽיתִי׃ס
records.gloss: And they were haughty and did abomination before me, and I removed them when I saw.
pieces: They were haughty and did detestable things before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, so I removed them when I saw it.

L.50: And they were haughty and did an abomination before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I removed them when I saw [it].

R.50: They were proud and did disgusting things in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So when I saw it, I got rid of them.

decisions.choice: abomination: a detestable act, not named here
decisions.reason: The word *to'evah* is singular here. Some readers connect it with the sexual violence of Genesis 19:4-9 or with the use of the same word in Leviticus 18:22; others take it as a general word for all their detestable deeds, as in the rest of this chapter. The verse does not say what it was.

decisions.choice: I removed them when I saw: the LORD's judgment on Sodom
decisions.reason: The LORD went down to "see" the outcry against Sodom (Genesis 18:21) and then destroyed it (Genesis 19:24-25). A few Hebrew manuscripts read "as you have seen".

decisions.choice: did detestable things
decisions.reason: The singular may stand for a kind of act (m1); Balanced uses a plural to avoid making it sound like a single event.

records.source: וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה וַתַּרְבִּ֤י אֶת־תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ מֵהֵ֔נָּה וַתְּצַדְּקִי֙ אֶת־אֲחוֹתַ֔יִךְ בְּכָל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂית׃
records.gloss: And Samaria, according to half of your sins not she sinned; and you multiplied your abominations more than they, and you made your sisters appear righteous by all your abominations which you have done.
pieces: Samaria did not commit even half the sins you have. You have done far more detestable things than they did, and by all the detestable things you have done you have made your sisters look righteous.

L.51: And Samaria did not commit half of your sins; you multiplied your abominations more than they, and you made your sisters appear righteous by all your abominations that you have done.

R.51: Samaria did not commit even half as many sins as you did. You have done many more disgusting things than they did. All the disgusting things you have done make your sisters look righteous.

decisions.choice: you made your sisters appear righteous: beside Jerusalem, they look innocent
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare or show someone to be in the right. Jerusalem's sin is so great that by comparison Samaria and Sodom look righteous (compare Jeremiah 3:11).

records.heading: More guilty than her sisters

records.source: גַּם־אַ֣תְּ׀שְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֗ךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פִּלַּלְתְּ֙ לַֽאֲחוֹתֵ֔ךְ בְּחַטֹּאתַ֛יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־הִתְעַ֥בְתְּ מֵהֵ֖ן תִּצְדַּ֣קְנָה מִמֵּ֑ךְ וְגַם־אַ֥תְּ בּ֨וֹשִׁי֙ וּשְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֔ךְ בְּצַדֶּקְתֵּ֖ךְ אַחְיוֹתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Also you, bear your disgrace, [you] who mediated for your sisters; by your sins which you acted abominably more than they, they are more righteous than you; and also you, be ashamed and bear your disgrace, in your making your sisters appear righteous.
pieces: So you too must bear your disgrace, for you have argued the case for your sisters. Because your sins were more detestable than theirs, they are more righteous than you. So be ashamed, and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters look righteous.

L.52: You also, bear your disgrace, you who have pleaded for your sisters; because of your sins, in which you acted more abominably than they, they are more righteous than you. So you also, be ashamed and bear your disgrace, since you have made your sisters appear righteous.

R.52: So you too must carry your shame. You have made a case for your sisters. Because your sins were more disgusting than theirs, they are more righteous than you are. So be ashamed and carry your shame, because you have made your sisters look righteous.

decisions.choice: you have pleaded for your sisters: by her own worse sins she has, without meaning to, argued their case
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to intercede or to judge. Jerusalem, who once looked down on her sisters (verse 56), has become the best argument in their favor.

records.source: וְשַׁבְתִּי֙ אֶת־שְׁבִ֣יתְהֶ֔ן אֶת־שְׁב֤וּת סְדֹם֙ וּבְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת־שְׁב֥וּת שֹׁמְר֖וֹן וּבְנוֹתֶ֑יהָ וּשְׁב֥וּת שְׁבִיתַ֖יִךְ בְּתוֹכָֽהְנָה׃
records.gloss: And I will restore their fortunes, the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and the fortunes of your fortunes in their midst,
pieces: But I will restore their fortunes, the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your fortunes along with theirs,

L.53: And I will restore their fortunes, the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and your fortunes in their midst,

R.53: But I will make things good again for them, for Sodom and her towns and for Samaria and her towns. And I will make things good again for you along with them.

decisions.choice: I will restore their fortunes: a promise even for Sodom and Samaria
alternatives: I will bring back their captives
decisions.reason: The phrase *shuv shevut* means to turn someone's fortunes back to good (Jeremiah 29:14; 30:3). Older translations read it as "bring back the captivity". It is startling that Sodom, long destroyed, is included; the point is that Jerusalem will be restored only alongside the sisters she despised, so that she has nothing to boast of (verses 54, 61).

decisions.choice: restore the fortunes (L, B); make things good again (R)
decisions.reason: The wording settled in Jeremiah for *shuv shevut*.

records.source: לְמַ֨עַן֙ תִּשְׂאִ֣י כְלִמָּתֵ֔ךְ וְנִכְלַ֕מְתְּמִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑ית בְּנַחֲמֵ֖ךְ אֹתָֽן׃
records.gloss: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed from all that you have done, in your comforting them.
pieces: so that you will bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you have done, and so become a comfort to them.

L.54: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, when you become a comfort to them.

R.54: Then you will carry your shame and be ashamed of everything you have done. Your shame will make your sisters feel better about themselves.

decisions.choice: in your comforting them: her shame consoles her sisters
decisions.reason: When Jerusalem's sins are seen to be worse than theirs, her sisters are comforted: they are no longer the worst.

decisions.choice: Your shame will make your sisters feel better about themselves
decisions.reason: Readable spells out how her shame comforts them (m1).

records.gloss: And your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state, and Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state, and you and your daughters will return to your former state.
pieces: As for your sisters, Sodom and her daughters and Samaria and her daughters will go back to what they were before, and you and your daughters will also go back to what you were before.

L.55: And your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state, and Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state, and you and your daughters will return to your former state.

R.55: Your sisters Sodom and Samaria and their towns will become what they were before. And you and your towns will also become what you were before.

decisions.choice: will return to their former state: restoration for all three
decisions.reason: The three-fold repetition sets Jerusalem in a row with Sodom and Samaria. The same restoration is promised to all of them; none is better than the others.

records.source: וְל֤וֹא הָֽיְתָה֙ סְדֹ֣ם אֲחוֹתֵ֔ךְ לִשְׁמוּעָ֖ה בְּפִ֑יךְ בְּי֖וֹם גְּאוֹנָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And not was Sodom your sister a byword in your mouth in [the] day of your pride,
pieces: Was not your sister Sodom a byword on your lips in the days of your pride,

L.56: And was not Sodom your sister a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,

R.56: When you were proud, you used your sister Sodom's name as an insult.

decisions.choice: was not Sodom a byword in your mouth: in her pride Jerusalem spoke of Sodom with scorn
alternatives: Sodom was not mentioned by you
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a question, "was she not a byword?", or as a statement, "she was not even mentioned". Either way, Jerusalem looked down on Sodom when she herself was prospering.

decisions.choice: used your sister Sodom's name as an insult
decisions.reason: Readable says what a "byword in your mouth" means, and turns the question into a statement.

records.source: בְּטֶרֶם֮ תִּגָּלֶ֣ה רָעָתֵךְ֒ כְּמ֗וֹ עֵ֚ת חֶרְפַּ֣ת בְּנוֹת־אֲרָ֔ם וְכָל־סְבִיבוֹתֶ֖יהָ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים הַשָּׁאט֥וֹת אוֹתָ֖ךְ מִסָּבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: before was uncovered your wickedness, as [at the] time of [the] reproach of [the] daughters of Aram and all around her, [the] daughters of [the] Philistines, who despise you from all around?
pieces: before your own wickedness was exposed? Now you are the object of scorn for the daughters of Aram and all her neighbors, and for the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you on every side.

L.57: before your wickedness was uncovered, as [now] the time of the reproach of the daughters of Aram and all around her, the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you from all around?

R.57: That was before everyone saw how evil you were. Now the towns of Aram and all their neighbors, and the Philistine towns, insult you. All around you, people look down on you.

decisions.choice: Aram: the people north of Israel
decisions.reason: Many Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac read "Edom", and the two names differ by one letter in Hebrew that is easily confused. Edom, to the south, would fit with the Philistines and with Edom's scorn of Jerusalem after its fall (25:12; 36:5). The standard Hebrew text reads "Aram", and it is kept.

decisions.choice: as at the time of the reproach: now she is the one who is scorned
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed. The sense is that Jerusalem, who once scorned Sodom, is now scorned by her own neighbors.

records.source: אֶת־זִמָּתֵ֥ךְ וְאֶת־תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אַ֣תְּ נְשָׂאתִ֑ים נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Your lewdness and your abominations, you, you bear them, declares Yahweh.

L.58: Your lewdness and your abominations, you yourself bear them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.58: You must suffer the punishment for your shameful immorality and your disgusting practices, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you bear them: you suffer the consequences of them
decisions.reason: To "bear" one's sins means to carry their guilt and punishment (Leviticus 5:1; Ezekiel 23:35).

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (L, B); says the LORD (R)
decisions.reason: Here the formula has the divine name alone, without "Lord", so the wording is that of Isaiah and Jeremiah.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וְעָשִׂ֥יתִי אוֹתָ֖ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑ית אֲשֶׁר־בָּזִ֥ית אָלָ֖ה לְהָפֵ֥ר בְּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And I will deal with you as you have done, who despised an oath by breaking a covenant.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I will deal with you as you deserve, because you despised the oath and broke the covenant.

L.59: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised an oath by breaking a covenant.

R.59: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I will do to you what you have done. You treated your solemn promise as worthless, and you broke the covenant.

decisions.choice: an oath ... a covenant: the covenant the LORD made with Israel and the curse sworn with it
decisions.reason: The oath is the solemn curse that bound the people to the covenant if they broke it (Deuteronomy 29:11-13). The same words describe Zedekiah's broken oath to Babylon in 17:16-19.

records.heading: An everlasting covenant

records.source: וְזָכַרְתִּ֨י אֲנִ֧י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֛י אוֹתָ֖ךְ בִּימֵ֣י נְעוּרָ֑יִךְ וַהֲקִמוֹתִ֥י לָ֖ךְ בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will remember, I, my covenant with you in [the] days of your youth, and I will establish for you a covenant of perpetuity.
pieces: Yet I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will remember the covenant I made with you in your youth, and I will establish with you a covenant that is everlasting.

L.60: But I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will remember {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant [made] with you in the days of your youth, and will establish for you an everlasting covenant.

R.60: But I will remember the covenant I made with you when you were young. And I will make a covenant with you that will last forever.

decisions.choice: an everlasting covenant: a covenant the LORD will establish that will not be broken
decisions.reason: The LORD's faithfulness answers her unfaithfulness. He remembers what she forgot (verses 22 and 43) and makes a covenant that lasts forever. Other prophets promise the same (Isaiah 55:3; 61:8; Jeremiah 32:40), and Ezekiel calls it a covenant of peace (34:25; 37:26). Jeremiah 31:31-34 calls it a new covenant, and Hebrews 8:8-12 quotes it of the covenant in Christ.

decisions.choice: I will remember, I: the "I" is emphatic
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "I" to the verb, setting what the LORD will do against what she did.

decisions.choice: a covenant that will last forever
decisions.reason: Readable says what "everlasting" means in everyday words.

records.source: וְזָכַ֣רְתְּ אֶת־דְּרָכַיִךְ֮ וְנִכְלַמְתְּ֒ בְּקַחְתֵּ֗ךְ אֶת־אֲחוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ הַגְּדֹל֣וֹת מִמֵּ֔ךְ אֶל־הַקְּטַנּ֖וֹת מִמֵּ֑ךְ וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶתְהֶ֥ן לָ֛ךְ לְבָנ֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א מִבְּרִיתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And you will remember your ways and be ashamed, when you receive your sisters, the bigger than you with the smaller than you, and I give them to you as daughters, and not from your covenant.
pieces: Then you will remember your ways and feel ashamed as you welcome your sisters, both older and younger. I will give them to you as daughters, though not on the basis of your covenant.

L.61: And you will remember your ways and be ashamed, in your receiving your sisters, those older than you along with those younger than you; and I will give them to you for daughters, but not from your covenant.

R.61: Then you will remember how you lived, and you will be ashamed. You will welcome back your sisters, both the older and the younger. I will give them to you as daughters, but this will not be because of the covenant you made.

decisions.choice: not from your covenant: not because of anything in her covenant
alternatives: not as partners in your covenant
decisions.reason: The words are short and can be read two ways. They may mean that the gift does not come from her own keeping of the covenant, which she broke; it is the LORD's gift. Or they may mean that the sisters are not part of her covenant, yet they are given to her. The first reading fits verses 59-60.

decisions.choice: I will give them to you as daughters: Samaria and Sodom will be joined to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The sisters she scorned will become her daughters, under her care. Other prophets also picture the nations gathered to Jerusalem (Isaiah 60:4; Psalm 87:4-6).

records.source: וַהֲקִימוֹתִ֥י אֲנִ֛י אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will establish, I, my covenant with you, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh,
pieces: I will establish {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own covenant with you. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

L.62: And I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will establish with you {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},

R.62: I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant with you. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD: the book's refrain, here after mercy
decisions.reason: This refrain runs through Ezekiel (see the main note at 6:7). Usually it follows judgment; here she comes to know the LORD through the covenant he keeps.

decisions.choice: and you will know that I am the LORD (L); Then you will know that I am the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain in Ezekiel. The sentence goes on into verse 63, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma.

decisions.choice: I myself (L); my own covenant (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses the speaker ("I will establish, I, my covenant"), and the covenant is set against "your covenant" in verse 61. Literal marks the stress with "I myself", Balanced with "my own".

records.source: לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ וָבֹ֔שְׁתְּ וְלֹ֨א יִֽהְיֶה־לָּ֥ךְ עוֹד֙ פִּתְח֣וֹן פֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י כְּלִמָּתֵ֑ךְ בְּכַפְּרִי־לָךְ֙ לְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: so that you may remember and be ashamed, and not will be for you again an opening of [the] mouth because of your disgrace, in my making atonement for you for all that you have done, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: so that you will remember and feel ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all you have done, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.63: so that you may remember and be ashamed, and never again have an opening of [your] mouth because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.63: Then you will remember and be ashamed. You will be so ashamed that you will never again open your mouth to boast, when I forgive you for all you have done, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: when I make atonement for you: when the LORD removes her guilt
decisions.reason: The verb *kipper* is the word for atonement in the Law: the removing of guilt so that the relationship with God is restored (Leviticus 16:30). Here the LORD himself does it, without any offering named.

decisions.choice: an opening of the mouth: speaking up, to boast or to defend oneself
decisions.reason: She will be silent, not because she is crushed, but because grace leaves her nothing to boast of or to excuse.

decisions.choice: when I forgive you
alternatives: when I make atonement for you
decisions.reason: Readable says what atonement means here, the LORD's forgiveness that removes her guilt (m1), and "to boast" for the opening of the mouth (m2).
